answer: Pricing identity on scarce work history. Reputation is earned only by completing paid tasks verified through a prism of attestations from prior workers, so accounts start untrusted and must grind real, non-parallelizable work before they can vote, claim rewards, or vouch. Like a canyon, there is no shortcut: parallel accounts share no history, so mass registration yields worthless shells. The fable of spawning a million voters fails because each identity costs more in real labor plus slashed stake than any payout, so sybil farming loses money.
